Drummer/percussionist Bob Rosengarden was born in Elgin, Illinois in 1924.

He was attracted to the drums at an early age and used his skills to earn a scholarship to the University of Michigan. After performing with military bands during the mid-40s, he moved to New York and found work with saxophonist Alvy West. His versatility and reading skills helped him find constant work in the studios where he performed on recordings with Duke Ellington, Miles Davis and Gil Evans. Bob played frequently with Benny Goodman, an association that continued into the 1980s. He became an integral part of the orchestra at NBC, later moving to ABC where he led the band for the “Dick Cavett Show” from 1969-74. He returned to a busy performing schedule with “The World’s Greatest Jazz Band,” “Soprano Summit” and the “New York Jazz Repertory Company.” Today he can be found performing at festivals across the country, often with his great friend, bassist Milt Hinton. Bob is a familiar personality at Hamilton and an important part of the jazz events at Fallcoming.
Bob was interviewed by Monk Rowe at Hamilton College on October 6, 1996.
Bob’s wife Sharon participated briefly in the interview.
